To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HE4 is overexpressed in ovarian cancer, is a novel nuclear protein that is regulated by hormones, interacts with ERα, and mediates nuclear translocation of ERα and is a novel regulator of antiestrogen resistance in ovarian cancer.

(a) 17β-estadiol, tamaxifen and fulvestrante induce HE4 nuclear translocation and HE4 over-expression induces resistance to anti-estrogens; (b) HE4 interacts with ER-α and downregulates ER-α in vitro and in ovarian cancers; (c) Importin-4 is involved in nuclear transport of HE 4 and ivermectine, an importin-4 inhibitor, blocks HE4/importin4
(1) HE4 expression is induced by antiestrogens and (2) HE4 overexpression results in antiestrogen resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HE 4 in the regulation of ovarian cancer cell responses to antiestrogen therapy and the potential for importin-α/β inhibitors to sensitize ovarian cancer cells to hormonal therapies.
a novel role of HE4, as a mediator of hormonal therapy response in ovarian cancer.
a novel mechanism by which ovarian cancer cells respond to hormonal agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HE4 protein is an important regulator of the estrogen response in human ovarian cancers and is an important target for ovarian cancer therapy.

our findings provide a mechanistic basis for understanding the role of HE in the pathophysiology of ovarian cancer and its response to hormonal therapy, which may have implications in developing new therapeutic strategies for this disease.
the expression of HE4 is associated with hormonal element, and HE4 expression is mediated by importin dependent nuclear translocation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HE4 is overexpressed in ovarian cancers and is regulated by hormones.

the nuclear localization and function of HE4 is regulated by the hormone 17β- estradiol and antiestrogens, and that the nuclear localization of HE4 is governed by the nuclear transport protein importin-4.
HE4 is an ER-α interacting protein that is regulated by estrogen and antiestrogens, and that HE4 is a potential target for ovarian cancer therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HE4 is a novel nuclear hormone receptor that mediates the effects of antiestrogens and that the nuclear transport of this protein is mediated by importin-4.
HE4 is an important regulator of ER-α expression in ovarian cancer and that HE4 nuclear translocation is mediated by importin-4.
HE4 expression is associated not only with hormonal elements, but that it also mediates the nuclear translocation of ER-α.
